faq: Why is a ZIP on two counties' lists?
A code may be present on addresses in more than one matched area; a result alone does not establish its delivery boundary. County names are not state-filtered.
USPS assigns each ZIP a preferred city name that can differ from the municipality the address sits in. The city slice follows postal naming and says so; civic truth lives with the boundary tools.
Codes serving one facility exist in the postal file; list tools vary in carrying them. For mailing work their absence rarely matters; for completeness claims, the note on the list governs.
How often do ZIP lists change?
USPS creates, splits and retires codes continuously as delivery grows. Any frozen list is a snapshot — for production mail, current CASS-grade data is the standard.
Can I get the list as a file?
The current workspace displays a result list; it does not offer a dedicated file export.
Different systems, different tools: Canada's FSAs and UK postcode districts live in the Location family's postcode tools, sliced their own ways.
The +4 refines delivery within a ZIP and multiplies the list a thousandfold — reference lists live at the 5-digit level, where geography still means something.
